note: Hebrew gevulot means boundaries/territory; "coasts" in 1611 meant borders, not seashores, which misleads a modern reader in this inland boundary list (also vv.3, 11, 12).
Hebrew nachal mitsrayim is a seasonal watercourse (usually identified with Wadi el-Arish), not the Nile, which "river of Egypt" suggests.
Hebrew levo' hamat may be "the approach to Hamath" or the town name Lebo(-hamath); the latter is now widely preferred since it sits in a list of place names.
Hebrew me'ever le-yarden literally "from beyond the Jordan", here the east bank; the KJV renders from the speaker's Transjordan standpoint, which obscures the term.
